attribution: Brewing-prepared adjuncts (flaked/torrified) use published brewing extract figures. Raw grains and rices have no brewing datasheet, so their PPG is derived from USDA FoodData Central nutrition data via lib/fermentable-math.ts — PPG = 46 x (total carbohydrate - fibre) / serving weight. The nutrition inputs are stored with each entry so the figure can be audited.

fermentables.name: Flaked Maize
fermentables.description: Pre-gelatinised corn flakes; lightens body and colour and dries the finish without cereal-mashing.
fermentables.usageNotes: Needs diastatic base malt to convert — no enzymes of its own.

fermentables.name: Flaked Rice
fermentables.description: Pre-gelatinised rice; the crispest, most neutral way to lighten a beer. The classic American macro-lager adjunct.

fermentables.name: Flaked Oats
fermentables.description: Adds silky mouthfeel, body, and haze. Essential in oatmeal stouts and modern hazy IPAs.
fermentables.usageNotes: Gummy beta-glucans — use rice hulls above ~20% to protect the sparge.

fermentables.name: Flaked Barley
fermentables.description: Unmalted flaked barley — big protein contribution for head retention and the creamy body of Irish stout.

fermentables.name: Flaked Wheat
fermentables.description: Unmalted wheat for witbier and lambic; haze, tang, and dense foam.

fermentables.name: Torrified Wheat
fermentables.description: Heat-puffed whole wheat; similar to flaked wheat, traditional in English ales.

fermentables.name: Long Grain White Rice
fermentables.description: Ordinary long-grain white rice. High-amylose starch that gelatinises around 158–172°F, so it needs a cereal mash before it will convert.
fermentables.usageNotes: Cereal mash: boil with ~20% of the base malt to gelatinise, then combine with the main mash.

fermentables.name: Sushi Rice (Short Grain)
fermentables.description: Short-grain japonica rice, high in amylopectin so it gelatinises at a lower temperature and goes sticky. The rice class used for sake.
fermentables.usageNotes: Lower gelatinisation point than long grain makes it a bit easier to cereal-mash.

fermentables.name: Arborio Rice
fermentables.description: Italian short-grain risotto rice, unusually high in amylopectin — it releases starch readily and can add a creamy body.
fermentables.usageNotes: Its free-starch tendency makes for a thick, gluey cereal mash; keep the volume generous.

fermentables.name: Jasmine Rice
fermentables.description: Aromatic Thai long-grain rice; carries a faint floral, popcorn-like aroma that can survive into the beer.

fermentables.name: Basmati Rice
fermentables.description: Long-grain aromatic rice with a nutty, tea-like aroma.

fermentables.name: Glutinous / Sweet Rice
fermentables.description: Almost pure amylopectin (no gluten despite the name). Used across Asian rice-wine and spirit traditions; very sticky when cooked.

fermentables.name: Brown Rice
fermentables.description: Whole-grain rice with the bran intact — nuttier, but the bran oil can hurt head retention and shelf stability.
fermentables.usageNotes: The oil content is a real staling risk; keep the percentage modest.

fermentables.name: Wild Rice
fermentables.description: Not a true rice (Zizania). Earthy, tea-like, and much higher in fibre, so lower extract.

fermentables.name: Corn Grits / Polenta
fermentables.description: Raw milled corn. Cheap extract and a soft sweetness; must be cereal-mashed to gelatinise the starch.
fermentables.usageNotes: The traditional pre-Prohibition American lager adjunct, and the backbone of bourbon mashes.

fermentables.name: Cracked Corn
fermentables.description: Coarsely cracked field corn — the base of bourbon and corn whiskey mashes (bourbon requires ≥51% corn).
fermentables.usageNotes: Cook to gelatinise, then convert with malted barley or exogenous enzymes.

fermentables.name: Quinoa
fermentables.description: Gluten-free pseudocereal; nutty and slightly grassy. Rinse well — the natural saponin coating is bitter and soapy.

fermentables.name: Millet
fermentables.description: A staple gluten-free brewing grain, and the traditional base of many African beers. Available malted for gluten-free brewing.

fermentables.name: Sorghum (Grain)
fermentables.description: Gluten-free grain used for African sorghum beers and, in China, as the primary grain for baijiu.

fermentables.name: Buckwheat
fermentables.description: Gluten-free pseudocereal with a strong earthy, almost tannic character.

fermentables.name: Rice Hulls
fermentables.description: Not a fermentable at all — an inert filter bed that keeps gummy grists (wheat, rye, oats) from sticking the sparge.
fermentables.usageNotes: Contributes zero gravity and zero flavour. Roughly 0.5–1 lb per 5 gal batch when needed.
